references.text: Describes the curtain for the entrance of the courtyard, made from the same materials: blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen, embroidered work.
The fulfillment of the command in Exodus 26:36, where the curtain for the tent entrance was actually made from the specified materials.
The inner curtain between the holy place and the Most Holy Place, made with the same colors and materials but with cherubim woven into it.
Describes the craftsmen who were filled with wisdom to perform embroidery work in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen.
The curtain for the gate of the courtyard, also made from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, embroidered work.
The responsibility of the Gershonites included the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle, showing the continued significance of this curtain.
Describes the structure of the tabernacle with the first tent and the curtain that separated the holy place from the Most Holy Place, a type of Christ's work.
The curtain as a type of Christ's body, through which we have boldness to enter the sanctuary.
Divisions in the sanctuary: Highlights the difference between the entrance curtain and the innermost curtain with cherubim.
Continuity in God's dwelling: Solomon's temple reuses the tabernacle's symbolism to show that God still dwells among His people.
